expressions.tmdl: /// Release tag of the data to load: data-1m-v1 or data-10m-v1
expression DataTag = "data-1m-v1" meta [IsParameterQuery=true, List={"data-1m-v1", "data-10m-v1"}, DefaultValue="data-1m-v1", Type="Text", IsParameterQueryRequired=true]
/// Loads one Parquet file from the GitHub release named by DataTag.
/// The base URL is a static literal and everything dynamic is in RelativePath,
/// so the service can refresh it without a dynamic data source error.
/// Timestamp columns arrive as UTC datetimezone; the zone is dropped so dates never shift.
List.Transform(ZoneColumns, (c) => {c, each if _ = null then null else DateTimeZone.RemoveZone(_), type datetime})
/// Staging, not loaded. Referenced by several loaded queries.
// ANTIPATTERN: every column, numbers and dates included, is turned into text
#"All Text" = Table.TransformColumnTypes(Source, List.Transform(Table.ColumnNames(Source), each {_, type text}), "en-US"),
// ANTIPATTERN: buffering here does not help; each loaded query that references this one evaluates it again
/// Staging, not loaded. Referenced by several loaded queries.
// ANTIPATTERN: every column, numbers and dates included, is turned into text
#"All Text" = Table.TransformColumnTypes(Source, List.Transform(Table.ColumnNames(Source), each {_, type text}), "en-US"),
// ANTIPATTERN: buffering here does not help; each loaded query that references this one evaluates it again
/// Staging, not loaded. Referenced by several loaded queries.
// ANTIPATTERN: every column, numbers and dates included, is turned into text
#"All Text" = Table.TransformColumnTypes(Source, List.Transform(Table.ColumnNames(Source), each {_, type text}), "en-US")
/// Staging, not loaded. Referenced by several loaded queries.
// ANTIPATTERN: every column, numbers and dates included, is turned into text
#"All Text" = Table.TransformColumnTypes(Source, List.Transform(Table.ColumnNames(Source), each {_, type text}), "en-US")
/// Staging, not loaded. Referenced by several loaded queries.
// ANTIPATTERN: every column, numbers and dates included, is turned into text
#"All Text" = Table.TransformColumnTypes(Source, List.Transform(Table.ColumnNames(Source), each {_, type text}), "en-US")
/// ANTIPATTERN (harmless): heavy, not loaded, referenced by nothing. Refresh never evaluates it.
Grouped = Table.Group(Buffered, {"CustomerKey", "StoreKey"}, {{"Lines", each Table.RowCount(_), Int64.Type}, {"Net Price", each List.Sum([NetPrice]), type number}})
model.tmdl: annotation PBI_QueryOrder = ["stg Sales","stg Customer","stg Product","stg Store","stg Date","Customer","Date","Product","Sales","Store","Currency Exchange","Sales Flat","Customer Stats","Unused Heavy Query","DataTag","fnLoadParquet"]
tables/Calendar Auto.tmdl: // ANTIPATTERN: second date table from CALENDARAUTO. Its range comes from every date column in the model (customer birthdays go back decades).
tables/Currency Exchange.tmdl: #"Changed Type" = Table.TransformColumnTypes(Source, {{"Date", type date}, {"FromCurrency", type text}, {"ToCurrency", type text}, {"Exchange", type number}})
tables/Customer Stats.tmdl: // ANTIPATTERN: Group By over the full fact in Power Query. CustomerKey repeats once per year, so the relationship to Sales is many-to-many.
#"Added Year" = Table.AddColumn(#"Buffered Rows", "Year", each Date.Year(DateTime.FromText([OrderDate], "en-US")), Int64.Type),
{"Sales Amount", each List.Sum(List.Transform(Table.ToRows(Table.SelectColumns(_, {"Quantity", "NetPrice"})), (r) => Number.From(r{0}, "en-US") * Number.From(r{1}, "en-US"))), type number}}),
tables/Customer.tmdl: #"Renamed Codes" = Table.RenameColumns(#"Added Name", {{"State", "State Code"}, {"Country", "Country Code"}, {"StreetAddress", "Address"}, {"ZipCode", "Zip Code"}}),

#"Selected Columns" = Table.SelectColumns(#"Renamed Names", {"CustomerKey", "Gender", "Name", "Address", "City", "State Code", "State", "Zip Code", "Country Code", "Country", "Continent", "Birthday", "Age"}),
// ANTIPATTERN: types fixed late, after the text staging step
#"Changed Type" = Table.TransformColumnTypes(#"Selected Columns", {{"CustomerKey", Int64.Type}, {"Birthday", type datetime}, {"Age", Int64.Type}}, "en-US")
tables/Date.tmdl: #"Renamed Columns" = Table.RenameColumns(Source, {{"YearQuarter", "Year Quarter"}, {"YearQuarterNumber", "Year Quarter Number"}, {"YearMonth", "Year Month"}, {"YearMonthShort", "Year Month Short"}, {"YearMonthNumber", "Year Month Number"}, {"MonthShort", "Month Short"}, {"MonthNumber", "Month Number"}, {"DayofWeek", "Day of Week"}, {"DayofWeekShort", "Day of Week Short"}, {"DayofWeekNumber", "Day of Week Number"}, {"WorkingDay", "Working Day"}, {"WorkingDayNumber", "Working Day Number"}}),

#"Selected Columns" = Table.SelectColumns(#"Renamed Columns", {"Date", "Year", "Year Quarter", "Year Quarter Number", "Quarter", "Year Month", "Year Month Short", "Year Month Number", "Month", "Month Short", "Month Number", "Day of Week", "Day of Week Short", "Day of Week Number", "Working Day", "Working Day Number"}),
#"Working Day Flag" = Table.TransformColumns(#"Selected Columns", {{"Working Day", each _ = "1", type logical}}),

#"Changed Type" = Table.TransformColumnTypes(#"Working Day Flag", {{"Date", type datetime}, {"Year", Int64.Type}, {"Year Quarter Number", Int64.Type}, {"Year Month Number", Int64.Type}, {"Month Number", Int64.Type}, {"Day of Week Number", Int64.Type}, {"Working Day Number", Int64.Type}}, "en-US")
tables/Product Date Grid.tmdl: // ANTIPATTERN: CROSSJOIN of Product and Date. 2,517 products x 4,018 days = 10.1M rows.
// ===== KNOB: FirstYear trims the date range. 2016 keeps all 11 years, 2021 keeps about half the rows.         =====
// ===== Do NOT add Store or Customer to the crossjoin: x74 stores = 750M rows, which fails on any capacity. =====
tables/Product.tmdl: #"Renamed Columns" = Table.RenameColumns(Source, {{"ProductCode", "Product Code"}, {"ProductName", "Product Name"}, {"WeightUnit", "Weight Unit Measure"}, {"Cost", "Unit Cost"}, {"Price", "Unit Price"}, {"SubCategoryKey", "Subcategory Code"}, {"SubCategoryName", "Subcategory"}, {"CategoryKey", "Category Code"}, {"CategoryName", "Category"}}),

#"Selected Columns" = Table.SelectColumns(#"Renamed Columns", {"ProductKey", "Product Code", "Product Name", "Manufacturer", "Brand", "Color", "Weight Unit Measure", "Weight", "Unit Cost", "Unit Price", "Subcategory Code", "Subcategory", "Category Code", "Category"}),

#"Changed Type" = Table.TransformColumnTypes(#"Sorted Rows", {{"ProductKey", Int64.Type}, {"Weight", type number}, {"Unit Cost", Currency.Type}, {"Unit Price", Currency.Type}, {"Subcategory Code", Int64.Type}, {"Category Code", Int64.Type}}, "en-US")
tables/Sales Copy.tmdl: // ANTIPATTERN: full copy of Sales, all columns including the calculated ones, plus RELATED columns.
// ===== KNOB: CopyCount = number of copies of the Sales rows. 1 copy = 2.35M rows on the 1M data. =====
// ===== Estimate per copy: +40 to 60 MB model size, +1.2 to 1.8 GB peak refresh memory.            =====
tables/Sales Flat.tmdl: // ANTIPATTERN: flat table. Sales merged with every dimension in Power Query (no folding on Parquet) and loaded next to the star.

#"Expanded Customer" = Table.ExpandTableColumn(#"Merged Customer", "C", {"GivenName", "Surname", "City", "StateFull", "CountryFull", "Continent"}, {"C.GivenName", "C.Surname", "Customer City", "Customer State", "Customer Country", "Customer Continent"}),
#"Expanded Store" = Table.ExpandTableColumn(#"Merged Store", "S", {"Description", "CountryName", "State"}, {"Store Name", "Store Country", "Store State"}),
#"Expanded Date" = Table.ExpandTableColumn(#"Merged Date", "D", {"Year", "YearMonth", "Month", "DayofWeek"}, {"Year", "Year Month", "Month", "Day of Week"}),
#"Added Customer Name" = Table.AddColumn(#"Expanded Date", "Customer Name", each [C.GivenName] & " " & [C.Surname], type text),
// ANTIPATTERN: concatenated text key, one distinct string per row
#"Added Order Line Key" = Table.AddColumn(#"Added Customer Name", "Order Line Key", each [OrderKey] & "-" & [LineNumber], type text),

#"Renamed Columns" = Table.RenameColumns(#"Added Order Line Key", {{"OrderKey", "Order Number"}, {"LineNumber", "Line Number"}, {"OrderDate", "Order Date"}, {"DeliveryDate", "Delivery Date"}, {"UnitPrice", "Unit Price"}, {"NetPrice", "Net Price"}, {"UnitCost", "Unit Cost"}, {"CurrencyCode", "Currency Code"}, {"ExchangeRate", "Exchange Rate"}}),

#"Selected Columns" = Table.SelectColumns(#"Renamed Columns", {"Order Number", "Line Number", "Order Date", "Delivery Date", "CustomerKey", "StoreKey", "ProductKey", "Quantity", "Unit Price", "Net Price", "Unit Cost", "Currency Code", "Exchange Rate", "Order Line Key", "Customer Name", "Customer City", "Customer State", "Customer Country", "Customer Continent", "Product Name", "Brand", "Category", "Subcategory", "Store Name", "Store Country", "Store State", "Year", "Year Month", "Month", "Day of Week"}),
#"Sorted Rows" = Table.Sort(#"Selected Columns", {{"Customer Name", Order.Ascending}, {"Order Line Key", Order.Ascending}}),
// ANTIPATTERN: only two columns get a real type. Keys, quantities, prices and the delivery date stay text.
#"Changed Type" = Table.TransformColumnTypes(#"Buffered Rows", {{"Order Number", Int64.Type}, {"Order Date", type datetime}}, "en-US")
tables/Sales Summary.tmdl: // ANTIPATTERN: summary of Sales as a calculated table. Roughly 1M rows on the 1M data.
// ===== KNOB: grain. Replacing 'Date'[Year] with 'Date'[Year Month] roughly doubles the rows. =====
tables/Sales.tmdl: measure 'Sales Amount' = SUMX ( Sales, Sales[Quantity] * Sales[Net Price] )
measure 'Total Cost' = SUMX ( Sales, Sales[Quantity] * Sales[Unit Cost] )
column 'Product Price Rank' = RANKX ( ALL ( 'Product'[Unit Price] ), 'Product'[Unit Price], RELATED ( 'Product'[Unit Price] ), DESC, Dense )
column 'Sales Line Label' = Sales[Product Category] & " | " & RELATED ( 'Product'[Brand] ) & " | " & Sales[Customer Country] & " | " & FORMAT ( Sales[Order Date], "yyyy-mm" )
column 'Customer Lifetime Sales' = CALCULATE ( [Sales Amount], ALLEXCEPT ( Sales, Sales[CustomerKey] ) )
// ANTIPATTERN: sort and buffer the full fact for no reason (and on text, so the order is not even right)

#"Renamed Columns" = Table.RenameColumns(#"Buffered Rows", {{"OrderKey", "Order Number"}, {"LineNumber", "Line Number"}, {"OrderDate", "Order Date"}, {"DeliveryDate", "Delivery Date"}, {"UnitPrice", "Unit Price"}, {"NetPrice", "Net Price"}, {"UnitCost", "Unit Cost"}, {"CurrencyCode", "Currency Code"}, {"ExchangeRate", "Exchange Rate"}}),
// ANTIPATTERN: line-level key, one distinct value per row
#"Added Order Line" = Table.AddColumn(#"Renamed Columns", "Order Line", each Number.From([Order Number]) * 10 + Number.From([Line Number]), Int64.Type),
// ANTIPATTERN: datetime with a time part. The source has dates only, so a synthetic time of day is derived from the order number.

#"Added Order DateTime" = Table.AddColumn(#"Added Order Line", "Order DateTime", each DateTime.FromText([Order Date], "en-US") + #duration(0, 0, 0, Number.Mod(Number.From([Order Number]) * 7919, 86400)), type datetime),

#"Selected Columns" = Table.SelectColumns(#"Added Order DateTime", {"Order Number", "Line Number", "Order Line", "Order Date", "Order DateTime", "Delivery Date", "CustomerKey", "StoreKey", "ProductKey", "Quantity", "Unit Price", "Net Price", "Unit Cost", "Currency Code", "Exchange Rate"}),
// ANTIPATTERN: types converted late, after sort, buffer and new columns

#"Changed Type" = Table.TransformColumnTypes(#"Selected Columns", {{"Order Number", Int64.Type}, {"Line Number", Int64.Type}, {"Order Date", type datetime}, {"Delivery Date", type datetime}, {"CustomerKey", Int64.Type}, {"StoreKey", Int64.Type}, {"ProductKey", Int64.Type}, {"Quantity", Int64.Type}, {"Unit Price", Currency.Type}, {"Net Price", Currency.Type}, {"Unit Cost", Currency.Type}, {"Exchange Rate", type number}}, "en-US"),
tables/Store.tmdl: #"Renamed Columns" = Table.RenameColumns(Source, {{"StoreCode", "Store Code"}, {"CountryName", "Country"}, {"Description", "Name"}, {"SquareMeters", "Square Meters"}, {"OpenDate", "Open Date"}, {"CloseDate", "Close Date"}}),
#"Selected Columns" = Table.SelectColumns(#"Renamed Columns", {"StoreKey", "Store Code", "Country", "State", "Name", "Square Meters", "Open Date", "Close Date", "Status"}),

#"Changed Type" = Table.TransformColumnTypes(#"Selected Columns", {{"StoreKey", Int64.Type}, {"Store Code", Int64.Type}, {"Square Meters", Int64.Type}, {"Open Date", type datetime}, {"Close Date", type datetime}}, "en-US")
